proposal: Register re-inspectors for chart.raster.curve_value_query.v1, chart.raster.curve_x_at_y_query.v1 and chart.raster.scene_graph.v1
decisive_question: Does checking that the reported anchor is ink of the declared colour also prove the reported value is the correct reading of that curve?
counterexample: An adapter can anchor honestly on real ink and still read the wrong value: report the correct pixel for a point on the curve, then return a value that does not follow from the axis calibration. The anchor check passes and the number is wrong. Likewise a curve of the right colour from the wrong series passes.
implication: These inspectors anchor the claim to real pixels and refuse fabrication; they do not verify the calibration arithmetic. The adapters' own hard_nonclaims list already declines semantic authority, and this receipt records that the independent check is narrower than the claim.
what_would_close_it: An inspector that recomputes the axis calibration from the tick marks independently of the adapter's calibration code, then re-derives the value. Not attempted here.
